content.text:
Yes. That post is visible. It is Dikshit Jain’s article, “If You Suck at SEO, Let Your AI Handle It,” posted 11 October 2026.

This site is still early: three public pages (`/`, `/privacy`, `/terms`), no Search Console, and no keyword data. I fixed the crawl and indexing problems in the repo. New articles would not help until these are live.

**What was wrong on the live site**

- A missing URL such as `/this-page-does-not-exist` returned a 307 to `/auth` instead of a 404, so Google was being sent to the sign-in page.
- `/auth`, `/dashboard`, and run pages could be indexed. Only Settings and onboarding were marked `noindex`.
- The homepage title, meta description, and social description disagreed with each other.
- There was no homepage structured data. Privacy and terms JSON-LD said they were modified on 10 October, while the pages say 12 October.
- The sitemap `lastmod` was 10 October for every URL, and it included `changefreq` and `priority`, which Google ignores.
- Closed FAQ answers and inactive “how it works” descriptions were missing from the HTML. Only the open item was present.

**What I changed**

- Unknown URLs now fall through to the 404 page. Only `/dashboard` and `/onboarding` still redirect to sign-in.
- Sign-in, the dashboard, and onboarding send `noindex`.
- The homepage title, description, and social tags now use one sentence, and the social image alt matches the image.
- Homepage JSON-LD is Organization, WebSite, and WebPage, matching the visible page. FAQ rich results were removed from Google Search in May 2026, so there is no FAQPage markup.
- Privacy and terms share one modified date, `2026-10-12`, in both the visible line and the structured data. The sitemap uses that date for those two URLs and `2026-10-10` for the homepage.
- FAQ answers and workflow descriptions stay in the HTML when collapsed. FAQ questions are now `h3`s under the section heading.
- These decisions are in the README “Already decided” section, with a re-check on 26 October and 9 November 2026.

The homepage already had one `h1`, a viewport tag, a self-referencing canonical, `robots.txt`, and footer links between the home, privacy, and terms pages. The “−6 pts” line in the hero is a product illustration, not a published result.

Typecheck passed. I did not start the dev server, so this is not on https://friction-fixer.shivamtaneja.com until you deploy. Search Console and Keyword Planner were not connected, so rankings, impressions, and search volume were not checked.
